title: Factory Method, Simple Factory and Abstract Factory

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Which design is the GoF Factory Method pattern rather than a Simple Factory?

options.text: A static create(type) method that switches on a type name to pick the class.
options.says: One static method choosing the class from a parameter is the Simple Factory idiom, which the page says is not the GoF pattern.

options.text: A static of() or from() method that hides a private constructor behind it.
options.says: Moving new into a static method is a static factory method; the page says the pattern is not just that.

options.text: A creator whose own logic calls a method each subclass overrides.
options.says: The pattern delegates instantiation to subclasses: the creator calls the factory method and a subclass decides the product.

questions.stem: What sets the Abstract Factory pattern apart from the Factory Method pattern?

options.text: It makes a family of related products through an object handed to clients.
options.says: Abstract Factory groups several creation methods in one factory object passed by composition, so the products match.

options.text: It makes a single product through a method that one subclass overrides.
options.says: One product from an overridden method is the Factory Method pattern itself.

options.text: It makes each product through a static method that tests a type name.
options.says: A static method with a conditional is the Simple Factory idiom, neither of the two GoF patterns.

concepts: Abstract Factory creates a family of related products through a factory object passed to clients, where Factory Method creates one product through a subclass override.
A static method choosing the class is a Simple Factory; the Factory Method pattern delegates instantiation to subclasses.
